decisions.rationale: The clinical presentation and imaging findings are consistent with primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL), which is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that arises in the brain or spinal cord.
Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma is a rare type of lymphoma that primarily affects the blood vessels, and the clinical presentation and imaging findings do not support this diagnosis.
Secondary CNS involvement by systemic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma would typically involve a known history of systemic lymphoma, which is not mentioned in the case.

Lymphomatosis cerebri variant of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a rare subtype of DLBCL that presents with diffuse brain involvement, which is consistent with the imaging findings in this case.
